newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Baan shares jump on Valmet order.
newsitem.headline: Baan shares jump on Valmet order.

text.p: Shares in Dutch/American software house Baan surged to an all-time high in heavy trade on Tuesday after Valmet Oy of Finland announced it had placed an order with it for an "exceptionally large" production control system.
Baan shares added 6.40 guilders to 102.50 at midsession, after opening up 2.50 at 98.60.
Valmet, a Finnish paper machinery group, said that according to Baan the order was similar in size to Baan's agreements with aviation giants Boeing and British Aerospace.
The Boeing order several years back was worth $20 million.
Contacted for details, Baan Nordic said it would not comment on the size of the order.
Analysts estimates of the worth of the contract varied from $10-$15 million to $25 million.
"This is certainly a substantially larger contract than usual," said Ruurt van der Torre, analyst with ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
He said Valmet had indicated it planned to have some 6,000 workers worldwide linked up to the system in the longer term, which would make the contract comparable in size to that placed by Boeing.
However, such projects were implemented in phases and the initial revenues were likely to be much smaller.
"There's no doubt it's a big order and an important boost for Baan's Scandinavian activities which were set up fairly recently," Van der Torre said.
Baan signed some 227 new contracts in the 1996 final quarter, of which 13 were worth over $1 million.
On average, the deals were worth some $0.32 million each.
